title: Linearity and object representatives for an additive localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], and equip $\mathcal C$ with an $R$-linear structure [def-weil-linear-category]. Let $W$ be a class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ and let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive functor (it preserves sums on each morphism group) which is a localization at $W$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Then $\mathcal D$ has a canonical $R$-linear structure for which $L$ is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor], so $L(rf)=rL(f)$ for every $r\in R$ and morphism $f$. Moreover $L(w)$ is an isomorphism for every $w\in W$, and every object $Y$ of $\mathcal D$ admits an object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ and an isomorphism $L(X)\cong Y$.
